uncited: It builds on the [Neural Scene Graph](14682-neural-scene-graph.md) structure, utilizing its directed acyclic graph definition to manage scene hierarchy.
The scene is represented as a directed acyclic graph.
*   **Dynamic Object Nodes:** Represent individual moving objects.
**Graph Construction:** Initialize the scene graph with a camera node, a background node, and dynamic object nodes.
**Shadow Assignment:** Assign the shadow of each object to its corresponding dynamic representation node.
**Rendering Isolated Static Components:** To render only the static background, remove all dynamic nodes from the graph.
**Rendering Isolated Dynamic Components:** To render only the dynamic foreground, exclude the static background node.
If the decomposition fails to separate static and dynamic elements correctly, isolation rendering will produce artifacts.
The sources do not specify numerical hyperparameters for the neural network optimization.
The quality depends on the ability to correctly identify and separate dynamic objects from the background.
Scaling to more complex scenes with higher object counts is not detailed in the sources.

It addresses the limitations of existing neural rendering techniques for dynamic environments, specifically the inability of SRNs to handle temporal changes and the ghosting artifacts of NeRF when camera poses vary.
The work demonstrates the flexibility of the neural scene graph representation by manipulating edges and nodes to preserve illumination cues and compose novel scenes.
